title: U.S. House · New Hampshire's 2nd District
area: Western and northern New Hampshire, including Nashua, Concord and Keene.

candidates.name: Maggie Goodlander

summary.text: Maggie Goodlander is the Democratic incumbent in New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in November 2024. A Nashua native, she worked as a Senate foreign policy advisor, Navy Reserve intelligence officer, Supreme Court law clerk, constitutional law instructor, Justice Department deputy assistant attorney general and White House senior advisor before running for Congress. She sits on the House Armed Services and Small Business Committees.

background.text: Born in Nashua, New Hampshire, in 1986; her House biography says she was raised in Nashua, where her family has lived for more than 100 years.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Yale University in 2009 and a J.D. from Yale Law School in 2016.
Began her career as a senior foreign policy advisor to U.S. Senators Joe Lieberman and John McCain; her House biography says she helped write sanctions legislation.
Served as an intelligence officer in the U.S. Navy Reserve for 11 years, according to her House biography.

After law school, clerked for Justice Stephen Breyer on the U.S. Supreme Court, then returned to New Hampshire to teach constitutional law at the University of New Hampshire and Dartmouth. Her House biography says she served as counsel in the first impeachment of President Donald Trump.

Served as a deputy assistant attorney general at the U.S. Department of Justice, where her House biography says she worked on cases involving corporate monopolies, and as a senior advisor at the White House, where she led the Unity Agenda (opioids, mental health, Big Tech, veterans, and cancer).
Won the September 10, 2024 Democratic primary for the open 2nd District seat over Colin Van Ostern, then defeated Republican Lily Williams 52.9% to 47.0% in the November 2024 general election.
Assigned in the 119th Congress (2025-2026) to the House Armed Services Committee (Military Personnel; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) and the Small Business Committee.
Has served as a board member of the NH Women's Foundation, NH Legal Assistance, and the World Affairs Council of New Hampshire, and on the Rudman Center Advisory Board.

positions.summary: Says she will defend access to the full range of reproductive healthcare, including abortion.
positions.quote: In Congress, Maggie will fight like hell to defend access to the full range of reproductive healthcare, including abortion, contraceptives, and IVF.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists protecting Medicare and the Affordable Care Act and expanding access to affordable healthcare among her priorities.
positions.quote: The fight for a fair deal means protecting Social Security, Medicare, and the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for closing tax loopholes for oil companies and a tax system with breaks for working families rather than for billionaires and large corporations.
positions.quote: It means building a tax system that works for hardworking Granite Staters by delivering tax breaks for working families – not handouts to billionaires and big corporations.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists raising the minimum wage among her priorities.
positions.quote: protecting the rights of workers, including to collectively bargain, and raising the minimum wage.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for combating climate change and making the U.S. a clean energy leader.
positions.quote: The fight for a fair deal also means combating climate change, standing up to Big Oil, and working to make America the world’s clean energy superpower.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Armed Services (Military Personnel; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) and the House Committee on Small Business (Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access; Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations; and Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Goodlander's official House website's issues page was unreachable (404) at the time of research, so stated priorities and issue positions beyond committee assignments were not located. Her key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Lily Williams

summary.text: Lily Williams is the Republican nominee for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District. Born in China, she taught law there before moving to the United States in 1988 and later worked as a social worker, corporate executive, consultant and real estate investor. She previously ran for office in Colorado as a Libertarian and ran in New Hampshire's 2nd District Republican primary in 2022 and general election in 2024; her campaign materials describe a government-reform platform including congressional term limits.

background.text: Born in Chengdu, China. In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey she describes growing up in China's Sichuan province during the Cultural Revolution.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Fudan University in 1985. She says she then joined the Fudan law faculty as an assistant professor and practiced corporate law in Shanghai.

Says she left China in 1988 to study at the University of Texas at Austin, where she earned a graduate degree in 1991 (she describes it as a master's in administration and planning from the School of Social Work).

Describes working as a medical social worker for Wyoming Home Health, then as an executive for corporations in Hong Kong and the United States, and later as a self-employed consultant and expert witness in China-related business and legal cases. She and her husband manage residential rental properties they own.
Ran as a Libertarian for the Colorado House of Representatives in 2014 and for U.S. Senate in Colorado in 2016.
In the 2022 survey she described herself as chair of the New Hampshire Asian American Coalition and an elected Supervisor of the Checklist in Weare, New Hampshire.

Finished third (24.6%) in the 2022 Republican primary for New Hampshire's 2nd District, won the Republican nomination in 2024, and lost the November 2024 general election to Maggie Goodlander, 47.0% to 52.9%. She won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary with 64.9%.

priorities.text: Her campaign describes a "10-Point Good Government Plan" that includes congressional term limits (three terms for U.S. House members, two for senators), requiring single-subject bills, ending funding by continuing resolutions, and banning stock trading by members of Congress.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for adequately funding ICE to enforce current immigration laws and ending catch-and-release.
positions.quote: We must enforce current immigration laws already on the books. ICE must be adequately funded and supported politically to enforce those laws. Catch and release policies must be terminated.

positions.summary: In an April 2026 interview, said she supports national constitutional carry and does not support red flag laws or more gun control.
positions.quote: I support national constitutional carry. Law-abiding citizens’ rights should not be infringed. Red flag laws and more gun control are not effective.

positions.summary: In an April 2026 interview, said she supports the SAVE Act requiring citizenship to register to vote.
positions.quote: I support the SAVE Act — citizenship required to register, and photo ID to vote.

candidates.researchNotes: Williams has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; priorities drawn from her campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia. No documented stance on the fixed issue list was found in the time available.

candidates.name: Robbie Mahrou

summary.text: Robbie Mahrou is an independent candidate for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District. According to Ballotpedia he works as a consultant; little additional biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Graduated from Strake Jesuit College Preparatory and earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University in 1999.
Lists his career experience as consultant; no prior elected office or earlier campaigns appear in the source.

priorities.text: Says the race comes down to affordability, accountability, and a government that follows the Constitution.
priorities.quote: This race comes down to three things. Affordability. Accountability. And a government that follows the Constitution again.

priorities.text: Protecting rural healthcare, including supporting the Break Up Big Medicine Act (S. 3822).
priorities.quote: Support the bipartisan Break Up Big Medicine Act (S. 3822), with protections for community health systems, first right to buy for local providers, and penalties sent back to rural pharmacies and hospitals

priorities.text: Supporting small-scale food processing and family farms.
priorities.quote: Back the PRIME Act so state and locally inspected processors can serve their communities

positions.summary: His platform calls for a 23 percent minimum tax on corporations with more than $5 billion in annual revenue.
positions.quote: A 23 percent minimum tax on corporations bringing in more than $5 billion a year

positions.summary: His platform calls for enforcing the War Powers Resolution so sustained military action requires explicit congressional approval.
positions.quote: Enforce the War Powers Resolution: require explicit congressional approval for sustained military action

positions.summary: His platform says he would oppose new federal restrictions on gun ownership by law-abiding citizens.
positions.quote: Oppose any new federal restrictions on law-abiding citizens' right to bear arms

positions.summary: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, answered For on a federal law guaranteeing the right to choose abortion before viability.
positions.quote: The right to make decisions about your own body is a constitutional right. No state or federal government has any business being on either side of that decision.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, answered For on limiting female sports participation based on sex at birth.
positions.quote: asking biological females to compete against biological males is not equality. It is an uneven playing field that undermines the very opportunities Title IX was designed to protect.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, said tariffs can serve a purpose if targeted and specific and enacted through Congress.
positions.quote: Tariffs can have a function in reshoring manufacturing and stimulating investment, but they must be targeted and specific and not result in American citizens paying yet another hidden tax.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, said he does not support Israel's current military campaign and that U.S. funding and weapons should not be part of it.
positions.quote: The United States cannot continue writing blank checks to a government operating under active ICC arrest warrants.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his campaign platform page and his 2026 Citizens Count Issue Survey responses (the page labels some answers For/Against; stances here are only recorded where his own words or answers address the issue). No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found.

statements.quote: I support enforcement that is constitutional, accountable, and reflects the will of the American people. Clear law. Consistent enforcement.
statements.context: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, on abolishing ICE

statements.quote: Return zoning and land-use decisions to local communities, not distant federal mandates

Energy is a national security issue and deserves a real strategy, one that includes expanding renewables and investments in emerging technologies, not doubling down on fossil fuel infrastructure with negligible net gain and permanent environmental risk.
statements.context: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey, on the Keystone XL pipeline

statements.quote: We have to acknowledge that the current system is broken and take a hard look at what the issue is. This has ultimately turned into a partisan blame game that results in Americans paying more to get less.
statements.context: In his 2026 Citizens Count survey (he marked For letting citizens opt into Medicare and Against automatic enrollment of every citizen in Medicare)
